question:

English:
generated_answer: Therefore, we introduced the 2022 Renters (Scotland) Act nearly 18 months ago, in an attempt to limit rents within a limited timeframe to alleviate the pressure brought on by the cost of living crisis. We have found from the latest statistics from the Scottish Government that all types of property saw an increase in average rents last year, with the lowest increase being 11.7% for one-bedroom properties and the highest increase being 14.3% for two-bedroom properties. Since the cost of living act came into effect in October 2022, rents for all types of properties, from one-bedroom to four-bedroom and single rooms, have seen double-digit increases, with the annual average rent increase being at least double that of the past 12 years.
ground_truth: Thus, we had the introduction of the Cost of Living (Tenant protection) (Scotland) Act 2022 nearly 18 months ago which sought to cap rents for a limited period to ease the pressures of the cost-of-living crisis. What we find now from the latest Scottish Government statistics is that, in the last year alone, average rents have increased in all sized properties, ranging from the lowest rise of 11.7 per cent for one-bedroom to the highest figure of 14.3 per cent for two-bedroom homes. Every type of property (from one to four bedroom to a room in a property) has had a double digit increase in rents since the Cost of Living legislation was introduced in October 2022, exceeding the annual average increases in rents over the previous 12 years by a factor of at least three.
